t:
Chapter 39 of title 10, United States Code, is amended—

    (1) 
by inserting the following new section after section 673:


“§ 673a. Ready Reserve: members not assigned to, or participating satisfactorily in, units

“(a) 
Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the President may order to active duty any member of the Ready Reserve of an armed force who—

“(1) 
is not assigned to, or participating satisfactorily in, a unit of the Ready Reserve;


“(2) 
has not fulfilled his statutory reserve obligation; and


“(3) 
has not served on active duty for a total of 24 months.



“(b) 
A member who is ordered to active duty under this section may be required to serve on active duty until his total service on active duty equals 24 months. If his enlistment or other period of military service would expire before he has served the required period under this section, it may be extended until he has served the required period.



“(c) 
To achieve fair treatment among members of the Ready Reserve who are being considered for active duty under this section, appropriate consideration shall be given to—

“(1) 
family responsibilities; and


“(2) 
employment necessary to maintain the national health, safety, or interest.”; and





 
    (2) 
by inserting the following item in the analysis:


“673a. Ready Reserve: members not assigned to, or participating satisfactorily in. units.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading keys on the word "participating," but here it refers only to reservists' satisfactory participation in their military units, not to outside parties taking part in a federal decision. The section authorizes the President to order certain Ready Reserve members to active duty and directs consideration of family responsibilities and employment. It provides no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: is not assigned to, or participating satisfactorily in, a unit of the Ready Reserve;

qwen_block.w: The term 'participating' here refers to the military service obligations of Reserve members, not to a process of public consultation or coordination with outside parties. The section describes the President's authority to activate reservists who are failing to meet their service requirements. There is no involvement of non-federal entities in a decision-making process, advisory capacity, or public comment period.
qwen_block.s: the President may order to active duty any member of the Ready Reserve of an armed force who— (1) is not assigned to, or participating satisfactorily in, a unit of the Ready Reserve;

opus.w: The section lets the President order certain Ready Reserve members to active duty and lists factors (family responsibilities, essential employment) to weigh. Those factors are criteria the government applies internally. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to object or sue. The word "participating" refers to reservists' unit service, so it is only a keyword match and not participation under the definition.
opus.s: To achieve fair treatment among members of the Ready Reserve who are being considered for active duty under this section, appropriate consideration shall be given to—
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the word "participating" appears ("participating satisfactorily in, a unit"), and subsection (c) requires "consideration" of family and employment circumstances. That reading fails. "Participating" here means a reservist's service in a military unit, not involvement in a federal decision. The "consideration" in subsection (c) is a set of factors the government weighs itself, with no consultation, hearing, comment period or right to object for anyone outside the government.

qwen_chat.w: The term 'participating' refers to military reservists fulfilling their service obligations within the armed forces. Since members of the Ready Reserve are part of the federal government (or subject to federal military authority), their service is an internal government matter, not consultation with outside parties. The section deals with active duty orders for non-compliant reservists, which is an administrative enforcement action, not public participation.
qwen_chat.s: is not assigned to, or participating satisfactorily in, a unit of the Ready Reserve
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The word "participating" appears in the text ("participating satisfactorily in, a unit"), which might suggest participation. However, this refers to military personnel fulfilling their service obligations within the armed forces, which is an internal government matter. The "participation" here is not consultation with outside parties but rather the performance of duty by federal employees (military reservists).
